features.title: Guía de pasajes
features.acceptance: Reunir comentarios, diccionarios y referencias pertinentes en un informe de pasaje; señalar fuentes ausentes.

implementation: Added a native passage guide that checks commentary resources and optional user-supplied dictionary/lexicon terms in priority order, searches explicit references across available resources, exposes source-backed opening and displays incomplete coverage and failures.
The guide publishes verified commentary results while reference scanning continues, names the current resource or reference-search phase, and cancels stale work when inputs, library, or view change.
Search explicit references concurrently with commentary and dictionary lookups; allow reference search across the library or one selected resource; preserve accent-sensitive dictionary terms.
Do not claim that explicit references were absent when a reference scan did not complete; show resource-opening failures in the guide itself.
Reuse the source-verified native dictionary entry count during search instead of recounting the database for every article; source stamps are checked around reads.
Use compact contiguous native-dictionary search directories and iterate descriptors lazily; preserve source-stamp validation, results, ordering and explicit coverage limits.
Keep source identifiers, coverage statuses and diagnostic details separately; localize status labels at display time without changing resource titles.
verification: Four PassageGuideControllerTests cover a real authored e-Sword commentary and explicit-reference scan, source identity, mixed results, incomplete coverage, failures, invalid input, partial results and cancellation. Existing KeyLinkControllerTests verify real dictionary and lexicon lookups and changed-source rejection.
Native build 137 displayed and opened the authored commentary while references were still being scanned. The user catalog and personal files were restored; the test resource was retained separately.

Six PassageGuideControllerTests pass, including concurrent partial results, accent-sensitive terms, a selected resource and missing-source handling. Native build 138 completed a scoped search against an authored commentary and opened the reference with its text selected. The test resource was removed and the original catalog and personal state restored.

Native build 138: the light Arabic interface displayed the initial form, scoped source and completed empty report with RTL headers and actions. Original English and automatic appearance settings were restored. Build 139 compiled the incomplete-report correction; its initial and searching states were inspected in dark appearance.

Native build 139: completed empty scoped report in dark appearance retained the accurate empty message. A whole-library search was cancelled after roughly one minute, with the process near 1.4 GB resident; cancellation returned the form to idle. This does not verify final partial-report rendering.

WorkspaceUnifiedSearchTests: seven executed tests passed, two corpus-dependent tests skipped; the dictionary test compares search projections with the original reader and validates count bounds. Native build 140 profiling of Spanish Wiktionary showed reference extraction and page reads, replacing the previous profile dominated by repeated SQLite COUNT operations.

Native build 140: a scoped search of the 837,661-entry Spanish Wiktionary reached the time limit, visibly marked reference coverage incomplete without claiming no references, and identified the partial source; a second search was cancelled successfully. Approximately 730 MB resident memory was observed during this single-resource run; it is not comparable to the earlier whole-library run.

Build 141 searched Spanish Wiktionary using a compact 837,661-entry directory; early process memory was approximately 200–225 MB versus approximately 770 MB observed in build 140 for the same scoped search. These are point observations, not controlled peak-memory benchmarks. PersistentLibrarySearchTests pass 13 tests including compact directory encoding and old identity decoding; WorkspaceUnifiedSearchTests compare source and indexed searches and exact citation results. A full test run passed 472 core tests and 46 BibliotecaMac tests; one topic concurrency test in the 460-test MacRebuild target failed under suite load and passed when rerun alone.

Build 141 reached the search time limit in the Spanish Wiktionary and displayed an incomplete reference report without claiming no matches. During the run, process resident memory was sampled at about 200–225 MB; results do not constitute a controlled peak-memory benchmark.

PassageGuideControllerTests and AppLanguageTests passed (13 tests), including a real incompatible-resource report and all status labels in ten languages. Build 143 displayed the same incomplete Wiktionary report in Spanish dark, Arabic light and English dark, preserving the resource name and updating the warning when the language changed. Original English/automatic settings were restored.
limitations: Long dictionary and library scans can still be slow; the guide displays partial matches and supports cancellation, but lookup duration is not independently bounded.
The guide uses user-supplied dictionary terms and explicit citation syntax; automatic terms from a passage and richer relationships are not yet implemented.
Narrow host-window, RTL results with actual matches, older macOS, complete-library time and memory consumption require further verification.
A single large dictionary search still uses substantial memory for its article directory and may reach its duration limit; this optimization removes repeated counting, not all search cost.
Diagnostic messages not supplied by the app catalog may remain in their source language; the status labels and known incompatible-resource explanation are translated.

implementation: Added named reference ranges with independently versioned, validated local storage and native creation, editing, deletion and selection. Named ranges can include or exclude Bible verses and are retained by search history and saved searches.
Changing a named range used by visible results invalidates those results until the search is run again. Missing named ranges report an error instead of silently widening the search.
verification: NamedBibleSearchRangesTests and BibleSearchRangeWorkflowTests passed for valid and invalid input, persistence, concurrent and future-schema protection, old configuration compatibility, actual Bible verse inclusion and exclusion, missing ranges and result invalidation.
Native build 173 was visually inspected in dark mode; a synthetic range was created, edited and selected, then test data was archived and the prior workspace restored.
limitations: Full comparison with original range-editor behavior and visual, keyboard, VoiceOver, light appearance, right-to-left and narrow-window acceptance remain pending.

implementation: Compact dictionary searches may now exclude only source-verified, indexed ASCII entries absent from the conservative candidate set, without materializing the whole directory. Unindexed and Unicode entries remain candidates.
verification: Search regression suites passed (36 core tests and 10 MacRebuild tests; two corpus-dependent cases skipped). A separate real bundled Easton test returned identical cold/warm hits: 3962 articles in 3.92 seconds cold, 2523 in 1.73 seconds warm, excluding 1439. A partial index, Unicode matches, short queries, and an index with a missing FTS row were exercised against linear results.

Native build 144: an Easton search returned 59 matching articles on both cold and warm runs, examining 3962 articles in 4.1 seconds and 2523 in 2.0 seconds respectively. Opening the first result selected the matching source text in the reader; the test reading and query were closed afterward.
limitations: The compact-index check retains metadata sets proportional to indexed entries; representative large, fully indexed libraries still need memory and long-session measurements.
